title: Putting Shapes Together and Taking Them Apart
seo_title: Grade 1 Composing Shapes Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 1)
standard_text: Compose and decompose triangles, squares, and rectangles.
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 worksheets on composing and decomposing shapes for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: put triangles, squares and rectangles together and take them apart. 100 questions with pictures and answers.
key_big: Two triangles can make a square.
key_sub: Color and size do not change a shape's name.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Two triangles can make a square or a rectangle.
  • Two squares side by side make a rectangle.
  • A rectangle can be cut into 2 squares or 2 triangles.
  • Color and size do not change the name of a shape. Sides and corners do.

Examples

Example

Two triangles

put the long sides together

Answer: a square

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Only the small shapesLook for big shapes too.
Color changes the shapeA red square is still a square.
Parts that are not the sameHalves must match.

faq.q: What does MATATAG Math 1 ask about composing shapes?
faq.a: Compose and decompose triangles, squares, and rectangles.
Two triangles, or four small squares.

faq.q: Can I make a triangle from two triangles?
faq.a: Yes, if they are the right shape.
They help children see shapes inside shapes.

items.q: This rectangle is made of 2 of which shape?
items.e: Look at the dashed line. Each part has 4 same sides and 4 square corners. 2 squares make the rectangle.

items.q: This square is made of 2 of which shape?
items.e: The dashed line goes from corner to corner. Each part has 3 sides. 2 triangles make the square.

items.q: Which 2 shapes make this rectangle?
items.e: The dashed line goes from corner to corner. Each part has 3 sides: 2 triangles.

items.q: How many triangles make this hexagon?
items.e: Count the triangles around the middle: 6. (3 is the number of dashed lines, not triangles.)

items.q: This hexagon is made of 2 of which shape?
items.e: Each half has 4 sides, and the long side is on the dashed line. 2 trapezoids make a hexagon.

items.q: How many triangles make this trapezoid?
items.e: Count the triangles: one points down in the middle, and one is on each side. That is 3.

items.q: Which shapes make this hexagon?
items.e: The bottom half has no lines inside: it is 1 trapezoid. The top half has 3 triangles.

items.q: How many small squares make this big square?
items.e: There are 2 small squares on top and 2 on the bottom. 2 + 2 = 4.

items.q: Which 2 shapes can make this rectangle?
items.e: Put 2 squares side by side and you get a long rectangle. Circles and hexagons do not fit together this way.

items.q: Which picture shows 2 triangles that make a square?
items.e: Picture D is a square cut from corner to corner, so it is 2 triangles. Another square is cut into 2 rectangles. One picture is a rectangle, and one is a triangle.

items.q: Put 2 squares side by side. Which shape do you get?
items.e: Shape B is a rectangle that is 2 times as long as it is tall. That is what 2 squares side by side make.

items.q: You put 2 triangles together. Which shape can you make?
items.e: Put 2 same triangles together along the long side and you can make a square. A hexagon needs more pieces, and a circle has no straight sides.

items.q: How many squares make this rectangle?
items.e: Count the parts between the dashed lines: 3 squares. There are 2 dashed lines, but 3 squares.

items.q: Lorna has 2 trapezoids. She puts the long sides together. What shape does she make?
items.e: 2 trapezoids with the long sides together make a hexagon, like pattern blocks.

items.q: Angelo makes hexagons. Each hexagon uses 2 trapezoids. He has 4 trapezoids. How many hexagons can he make?
items.e: 2 trapezoids make 1 hexagon. 2 more make another one. 2 + 2 = 4, so Angelo can make 2 hexagons.

items.q: Which 2 shapes make this house?
items.e: The bottom has 4 same sides and square corners: a square. The roof has 3 sides: a triangle.

items.q: How many small triangles make this big triangle?
items.e: There is 1 at the top, 2 at the bottom corners and 1 in the middle that points down. 1 + 2 + 1 = 4.

items.q: This circle is made of 2 of which shape?
items.e: The dashed line cuts the circle into 2 same parts. Each part is a half circle.

items.q: How many more triangles do you need to finish the hexagon?
items.e: A hexagon needs 6 triangles. There are 4. 6 − 4 = 2 more.

items.q: Which shapes make this trapezoid?
items.e: The middle part has 4 same sides and square corners: 1 square. Each end has 3 sides: 2 triangles.

items.q: Andrea makes a house. Which 2 shapes does she use?
items.e: The wall has 4 sides the same length. It is a square. The roof has 3 sides. It is a triangle.

items.q: Kenneth makes a rocket with shapes. How many triangles are there?
items.e: The tip is 1 triangle. There are 2 more at the bottom. 1 + 2 = 3 triangles.

items.q: How many triangles are in this sun?
items.e: Count the points around the circle. Each one is a triangle. There are 6 triangles.

items.q: Renz makes a train. How many circles does he use?
items.e: The wheels are circles. Count them: 4 circles.

items.q: Maria makes a robot with shapes. How many shapes are there in all?
items.e: Head 1, body 1, arms 2, legs 2. 1 + 1 + 2 + 2 = 6 shapes.
The boat is a half circle, the pole is a thin rectangle and the sail is a triangle. There is no circle.

c: a square and a half circle
a triangle and a half circle
a triangle and a quarter circle
items.e: The cone has 3 straight sides. It is a triangle. The top has 1 straight side and 1 curved side. It is a half circle.

items.q: How many small triangles make this kite?
items.e: The 2 lines cross in the middle. They make 4 small triangles.

items.q: How many small triangles make this big triangle?
items.e: There are 3 small triangles pointing up. Do not miss the one in the middle. It points down. 3 + 1 = 4.

items.q: Rafael cuts a rectangle along the line. How many triangles does he get?
items.e: The line goes from corner to corner. It makes 2 triangles.
There is 1 half circle on each side of the square. There are 4 half circles.

items.q: How many circles make this caterpillar?
items.e: Count the round parts: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. There are 5 circles.

items.q: What shape do these 2 triangles make?
items.e: Together they have 4 sides the same length and 4 square corners. They make a square.

items.q: Jomar puts 2 squares side by side. What shape does he make?
items.e: The new shape has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. It is a rectangle, not a square.

items.q: How many small squares make this big square?
items.e: There are 3 rows. Each row has 3 squares. 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. Do not miss the one in the middle.

items.q: Joy draws a tree. Which 2 shapes does she use?
items.e: The top has 3 straight sides. It is a triangle. The trunk has 2 long sides and 2 short sides. It is a rectangle.

c: a half circle and a triangle
a half circle and a rectangle
a quarter circle and a rectangle
items.e: The top has 1 straight side and 1 curved side. It is a half circle. The handle is a thin rectangle.

items.q: Which figure uses 3 triangles?
items.e: B is the rocket. It has 1 triangle at the top and 2 at the bottom. That is 3 triangles.
C is the ice cream. The cone is a triangle and the top is a half circle.
D is the sun. Its middle is a circle. The boat, the ice cream and the flower use half circles, not circles.

items.q: This circle is cut into 2 equal parts. What is each part?
items.e: 2 equal parts of a circle are 2 half circles.

items.q: This circle is cut into 4 equal parts. What is each part?
items.e: 4 equal parts of a circle are 4 quarter circles. A quarter circle has a curved side, so it is not a triangle.
1 half circle + 1 half circle = 1 circle. 2 half circles make a circle.
4 quarter circles fit together to make 1 circle.
A half circle is 2 quarters of a circle. 2 quarter circles make a half circle.
The 2 straight sides meet. The new shape has 1 straight side and 1 curved side. It is a half circle.
The 2 straight sides meet in the middle. The new shape is round all the way. It is a circle.
A circle is 2 half circles. Joshua has 1. 2 − 1 = 1 more.
C has 1 straight side. It is a half circle. Each quarter circle has 2 straight sides.
D is half of a circle, upside down. It has 1 straight side and 1 curved side.
A has 2 straight sides and 1 curved side. It is a quarter circle. The half circles have only 1 straight side.
B has a square corner and a curved side. It is a quarter circle. The triangle has 3 straight sides.

items.q: Which circle is cut into 2 half circles?
items.e: In D the line goes through the middle. The 2 parts are equal. The other cuts make parts that are not equal, or 4 parts.

items.q: Which circle is cut into 4 quarter circles?
items.e: In C both lines go through the middle. The 4 parts are equal. They are quarter circles.

items.q: Lance cuts a round pizza into 4 equal slices. What shape is each slice?
items.e: A circle cut into 4 equal parts gives 4 quarter circles. Each slice is a quarter circle.

items.q: Janelle cuts a round pancake into 2 equal parts. What shape is each part?
items.e: A circle cut into 2 equal parts gives 2 half circles.
Half of a half circle is a quarter circle.

items.q: Bianca cuts a circle like this. Are the 2 parts half circles?
c: No, the parts are not equal
items.e: Half circles are 2 equal parts. The line does not go through the middle. One part is bigger.
A half circle has 1 straight side. There are 3 half circles. The others are quarter circles and a circle.
A quarter circle has 2 straight sides and a square corner. There are 3 quarter circles.
In A every side is as long as in the figure. In the others one side is too long or too short.
The figure is 3 spaces long and 2 spaces tall. Only D is the same. Count the spaces, not the dots.
The figure goes 3 spaces down and 2 spaces across. Only C matches.
B has the same top and the same middle part as the figure. Check each side, one at a time.
C has the same roof and the same walls. One wrong copy has no roof, and others are too tall or too big.
The figure has 3 steps, each 1 space. Only B is the same.
The top of the figure is right above the middle of the bottom. The bottom is 4 spaces long. Only D matches.
Join both ends to dot A. All 4 corners are square corners and all 4 sides are the same length.

items.q: Nicole draws 2 sides of a rectangle. Which dot finishes the rectangle?
items.e: Join both ends to dot C. All 4 corners are square corners.
Join both ends to dot D. All 4 corners are square corners and all 4 sides are the same length.

items.q: Gabriel draws 2 sides of a rectangle. Which dot finishes the rectangle?
items.e: Join both ends to dot A. All 4 corners are square corners.
Join both ends to dot B. All 4 corners are square corners and all 4 sides are the same length.
C has 4 sides that are each 3 spaces long. It is a square. The shape 4 spaces long and 3 spaces tall is a rectangle.
A stands on a corner. Its 4 sides are the same length and its corners are square corners. It is a square. The thin one is not.
B has 4 straight sides and 4 square corners. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle.
D has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. It is a triangle, even when it is turned.
Each side goes 2 across and 1 up or down, so all 4 sides are the same length. The corners are square corners. It is a square.
It has 3 straight sides and 3 corners. It is a triangle. A quarter circle has a curved side.
It is 2 spaces across and 4 spaces down. 2 sides are long and 2 are short. It is a rectangle.

items.q: Bianca draws a house on dot paper. Which 2 shapes make it?
c: a square and a half circle
items.e: The bottom is 2 spaces each way. It is a square. The roof has 3 straight sides. It is a triangle.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: It is closed and has 3 straight sides. It is a triangle. Its size and color do not matter.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: Look at the corner with the gap. The sides do not meet, so the shape is open. A triangle must be closed.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: One side is curved. A triangle has 3 straight sides, so this is not a triangle.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: It has 3 straight sides and it is closed. It points down, but turning does not change the shape.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: It is small, but it is closed and has 3 straight sides. Small triangles are still triangles.

items.q: Is this a triangle?
items.e: Count the sides: 4. A triangle has only 3 sides. This shape is a trapezoid.

items.q: Which one is a triangle?
items.e: Shape C is closed and has 3 straight sides. One shape is open, one has a curved side and one has 4 sides.

items.q: Which one is NOT a triangle?
items.e: Shape A is open: 2 sides do not meet. The other three are closed with 3 straight sides. Their colors, sizes and turns do not matter.

items.q: Both shapes are triangles. What is different?
items.e: Both have 3 sides and 3 corners. Only the color, the size and the turn are different. These do not change the shape.

items.q: Is this a square?
items.e: It has 4 sides that are the same length and 4 square corners. It is a square standing on a corner.

items.q: Is this a rectangle?
items.e: It has 4 sides, but it leans over. Its corners are not square corners. A rectangle needs 4 square corners.

items.q: Is this a square?
items.e: There is a gap at one corner. The sides do not all meet, so it is open. A square must be closed.

items.q: Are shape A and shape B both hexagons?
items.e: Count the sides: A has 6 and B has 6. Both are hexagons. Size, color and side lengths do not matter.

items.q: Which one can change the name of a shape?
items.e: The name comes from the sides and corners. Color, size and turning never change the name.

items.q: Bianca colors a triangle blue. What shape is it now?
items.e: Color does not change a shape. It still has 3 sides, so it is still a triangle.

items.q: Bryan draws a big square. Mae draws a small square. Are they both squares?
items.e: Both have 4 same sides and 4 square corners. Size does not matter.

items.q: What does every triangle have?
items.e: Every triangle is closed and has 3 straight sides. It can point any way, and its sides can be different lengths.

items.q: Andrea draws 3 straight lines. The ends do not all meet. Is it a triangle?
items.e: The lines must meet at every corner to make a closed shape. With a gap, it is not a triangle.

items.q: Rose turns a square on its corner. She says it is a diamond now. Is she right?
items.e: Turning does not change a shape. It still has 4 same sides and 4 square corners. It is a square.

items.q: What does every rectangle have?
items.e: Every rectangle is closed with 4 sides and 4 square corners. It can stand up, lie down or be any color.
